questions.question: Which statement best describes communication in a computer networking context?
options: Only sending voice messages between people
Exchange of information, ideas, or data between sender and receiver using a method or medium
Storage of data permanently in a hard disk
Conversion of analog signal into digital signal only
questions.answer: Exchange of information, ideas, or data between sender and receiver using a method or medium
questions.correctAnswer: Exchange of information, ideas, or data between sender and receiver using a method or medium
questions.explanation:
Communication is the exchange of information between parties.
In networking, it normally happens through a channel and follows rules.

questions.question: In data communication, which element decides the rules for successful transmission?
questions.explanation:
A protocol is the set of rules used during communication.
TCP/IP is an example used on the Internet.

questions.question: A phone sends a photo to another phone using Wi-Fi. In this example, the photo is the:
questions.explanation:
The message is the actual data being transmitted.
It can be text, image, audio, or video.

questions.question: Which option correctly matches data communication and telecommunication?
options: Data communication is only human speech; telecommunication is only file transfer
Data communication transfers data between devices; telecommunication covers distance communication using technology
Both are exactly same and have no difference
questions.answer: Data communication transfers data between devices; telecommunication covers distance communication using technology
questions.correctAnswer: Data communication transfers data between devices; telecommunication covers distance communication using technology
questions.explanation:
Data communication focuses on device-to-device data transfer.
Telecommunication is broader communication over distance.

questions.question: Which transmission mode is most suitable for ordinary telephone calls?
questions.explanation:
In full-duplex mode, both sides can send and receive at the same time.
Telephone and video calls use this idea.

questions.question: A walkie-talkie allows both users to talk, but not at the same time. Which mode is this?
questions.explanation:
Half-duplex allows communication in both directions but only one direction at a time.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which example best represents simplex communication?
questions.explanation:
Simplex communication is one-way only.
A TV broadcast sends signals to viewers without receiving a reply through the same channel.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of broadband over dial-up Internet?
options: It only works with radio waves
It provides high-speed data transfer and allows large data to be sent/received quickly
It does not need any device
It prevents all network errors automatically
questions.answer: It provides high-speed data transfer and allows large data to be sent/received quickly
questions.correctAnswer: It provides high-speed data transfer and allows large data to be sent/received quickly
questions.explanation:
Broadband is much faster than dial-up and supports large data transfer.
It is useful for videos, online classes, and downloads.

questions.question: Which broadband type uses light signals through glass or plastic strands?
questions.explanation:
Fiber-optic broadband transmits data as light signals.
It provides high speed and reliable long-distance transmission.

questions.question: Why does satellite broadband usually have higher latency than fiber broadband?
options: It uses very short copper wires
The signal travels a long distance to and from satellites
It does not use electromagnetic signals
questions.answer: The signal travels a long distance to and from satellites
questions.correctAnswer: The signal travels a long distance to and from satellites
questions.explanation:
Satellite signals travel to space and back.
This long path creates more delay compared to fiber or cable systems.

questions.question: If an internet plan offers 100 Mbps but actual download speed is 60 Mbps, 60 Mbps is called:
questions.explanation:
Throughput is the actual amount of data successfully transferred per second.
Bandwidth is the maximum capacity.

questions.question: Which statement best compares bandwidth and throughput?
options: Bandwidth is actual speed; throughput is cable length
Bandwidth is maximum capacity; throughput is actual successful data transfer rate
Both always have the same value
Throughput is measured in hertz only
questions.answer: Bandwidth is maximum capacity; throughput is actual successful data transfer rate
questions.correctAnswer: Bandwidth is maximum capacity; throughput is actual successful data transfer rate
questions.explanation:
Bandwidth is the theoretical capacity of the channel.
Throughput is real-world performance.

questions.question: Which unit is commonly used to measure bandwidth?
questions.explanation:
Bandwidth is measured in bps, Kbps, Mbps, or Gbps.
These units show data transfer capacity.

questions.question: A large video is divided into many small parts before being sent over the Internet. These small parts are called:
questions.explanation:
Data packets are small units of data sent individually across a network.
They are reassembled at the destination.

questions.question: Which part of a data packet contains the actual content being transmitted?
questions.explanation:
Payload is the actual data.
Header contains addressing information and footer helps with checking errors.

questions.question: Why is a packet header important?
options: It stores only the cable color
It contains source, destination, and packet information
It converts digital signals to analog
questions.answer: It contains source, destination, and packet information
questions.correctAnswer: It contains source, destination, and packet information
questions.explanation:
The header helps the network know where the packet comes from and where it should go.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Frequency in telecommunication means:
options: Number of devices in a LAN
How often a signal repeats or is sent per second
questions.answer: How often a signal repeats or is sent per second
questions.correctAnswer: How often a signal repeats or is sent per second
questions.explanation:
Frequency shows how many cycles or signal repetitions occur per second.
It is measured in Hz, kHz, MHz, or GHz.

questions.question: Which frequency range is commonly associated with Wi-Fi mentioned in the notes?
questions.explanation:
Wi-Fi commonly works on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz frequency bands.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which mobile generation best supports smart devices, IoT, VR, and very high speed?
questions.explanation:
5G is faster than 4G and is designed to support many modern smart devices and applications.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which generation is correctly matched with typical use from the notes?
options: 3G - smart cities and VR as main use
4G - HD video streaming and online gaming with low lag
questions.answer: 4G - HD video streaming and online gaming with low lag
questions.correctAnswer: 4G - HD video streaming and online gaming with low lag
questions.explanation:
4G LTE is suitable for HD video streaming and online gaming with lower lag compared to 3G.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Communication media is also called:
questions.explanation:
Communication media is the path or channel through which information travels.
It is also called transmission media.

questions.question: Which option contains only guided media?
options: Twisted pair cable, coaxial cable, fiber optic cable
questions.answer: Twisted pair cable, coaxial cable, fiber optic cable
questions.correctAnswer: Twisted pair cable, coaxial cable, fiber optic cable
questions.explanation:
Guided media uses physical wires or cables.
Twisted pair, coaxial, and fiber optic cables are examples.

questions.question: Unguided media sends data mainly through:
options: Air, vacuum, or space as electromagnetic waves
questions.answer: Air, vacuum, or space as electromagnetic waves
questions.correctAnswer: Air, vacuum, or space as electromagnetic waves
questions.explanation:
Unguided media is wireless.
It transmits data using electromagnetic waves through air or space.

questions.question: Which statement is true about CAT6 cable?
options: It is a wireless satellite system
It uses RJ-45 connector and can support high Ethernet speed
It is used only for television broadcasting
questions.answer: It uses RJ-45 connector and can support high Ethernet speed
questions.correctAnswer: It uses RJ-45 connector and can support high Ethernet speed
questions.explanation:
CAT6 is a network cable used with RJ-45 connectors.
It can support 1 Gbps over 100 meters and higher speed over shorter distances.

questions.question: Why is CAT6 more reliable than older Ethernet cables like CAT5e?
options: It has better insulation and tighter twisted wires to reduce interference
It uses satellites instead of wires
questions.answer: It has better insulation and tighter twisted wires to reduce interference
questions.correctAnswer: It has better insulation and tighter twisted wires to reduce interference
questions.explanation:
CAT6 has improved construction that reduces signal interference.
This helps stable communication.

questions.question: Which connector is commonly used with CAT6 Ethernet cable?
questions.explanation:
RJ-45 is the common 8-pin connector used with Ethernet cables like CAT5 and CAT6.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Fiber optic cable transmits data using:
questions.explanation:
Fiber optic cable uses light signals through glass or plastic fibers.
This gives very high speed and long-distance support.

questions.question: Which pair contains common optical fiber connectors mentioned in the notes?
questions.explanation:
ST and SC are common optical fiber connectors.
SMA is also mentioned.

questions.question: Which medium is least affected by electromagnetic interference?
questions.explanation:
Fiber optic uses light rather than electrical signals.
It is highly resistant to electromagnetic interference.

questions.question: Which is the best definition of Wi-Fi?
options: A wired cable for Ethernet only
A wireless technology that connects devices to Internet/network using radio signals
questions.answer: A wireless technology that connects devices to Internet/network using radio signals
questions.correctAnswer: A wireless technology that connects devices to Internet/network using radio signals
questions.explanation:
Wi-Fi connects devices wirelessly using radio signals.
It commonly works through access points or routers.

questions.question: Bluetooth is most suitable for:
options: Short-distance wireless data sharing between nearby devices
questions.answer: Short-distance wireless data sharing between nearby devices
questions.correctAnswer: Short-distance wireless data sharing between nearby devices
questions.explanation:
Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology.
It is common in headphones, keyboards, speakers, and smartphones.

questions.question: Which technique helps Bluetooth reduce signal problems?
questions.explanation:
The notes mention FHSS as a smart method used by Bluetooth to avoid signal problems.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: RFID mainly uses:
options: Radio waves between tags and readers
questions.answer: Radio waves between tags and readers
questions.correctAnswer: Radio waves between tags and readers
questions.explanation:
RFID uses radio waves to transfer data between RFID tags and readers.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence in satellite communication?
options: Ground station uplink -> satellite receives/amplifies -> downlink to Earth
questions.answer: Ground station uplink -> satellite receives/amplifies -> downlink to Earth
questions.correctAnswer: Ground station uplink -> satellite receives/amplifies -> downlink to Earth
questions.explanation:
A ground station sends uplink to satellite.
The satellite amplifies and sends downlink back to Earth.

questions.question: Which use is NOT normally listed for satellite communication in the notes?
options: Connecting RJ-45 to CAT6 cable only
questions.answer: Connecting RJ-45 to CAT6 cable only
questions.correctAnswer: Connecting RJ-45 to CAT6 cable only
questions.explanation:
RJ-45/CAT6 connection is a wired networking issue, not a satellite communication use.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which statement best differentiates guided and unguided media?
options: Guided uses air; unguided uses wires
Guided uses physical cables; unguided uses wireless waves
Unguided is always unaffected by weather
questions.answer: Guided uses physical cables; unguided uses wireless waves
questions.correctAnswer: Guided uses physical cables; unguided uses wireless waves
questions.explanation:
Guided media has a fixed physical path.
Unguided media transmits through air or space.

questions.question: Which guided medium is usually best for very long distance and high bandwidth?
questions.explanation:
Fiber optic supports long distances and very high bandwidth.
ISPs widely use it for fast Internet.

questions.question: Which unguided medium can be affected by weather more than guided cables?
questions.explanation:
Wireless signals travel through air or space.
Weather conditions can affect some unguided transmissions.

questions.question: A school wants stable wired connections between computer lab PCs and a switch. Which medium is most suitable?
questions.explanation:
CAT6 Ethernet cable is appropriate for wired LAN connections to switches/routers.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which media type provides a fixed path for data transmission?
questions.explanation:
Guided media uses physical cables and provides a fixed route/path for signals.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A connector in networking is used mainly to:
questions.explanation:
Connectors are small hardware parts used to connect communication media to devices like computers, switches, and routers.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: RJ-45 is best described as:
options: An 8-pin Ethernet connector used in LANs
questions.answer: An 8-pin Ethernet connector used in LANs
questions.correctAnswer: An 8-pin Ethernet connector used in LANs
questions.explanation:
RJ-45 is an 8-pin connector used with Ethernet cables such as CAT5 and CAT6.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A media converter is needed when:
options: A network must convert signals between copper cable and fiber optic cable
A user wants to type faster
questions.answer: A network must convert signals between copper cable and fiber optic cable
questions.correctAnswer: A network must convert signals between copper cable and fiber optic cable
questions.explanation:
A media converter changes data signals from one transmission medium to another, such as copper to fiber.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which advantage correctly explains the need for a media converter?
options: It reduces all network security needs
It extends network distance by using fiber optic support
It changes IPv4 into IPv6 automatically
questions.answer: It extends network distance by using fiber optic support
questions.correctAnswer: It extends network distance by using fiber optic support
questions.explanation:
Fiber optic supports longer distances than copper.
A media converter helps extend the network.

questions.question: A networking device is hardware used to:
options: Connect devices so they can communicate and share data
questions.answer: Connect devices so they can communicate and share data
questions.correctAnswer: Connect devices so they can communicate and share data
questions.explanation:
Networking devices connect computers and other devices in a network for communication and resource sharing.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which device broadcasts received data to all ports and is now mostly replaced by switches?
questions.explanation:
A hub broadcasts data to the entire network.
Switches are more efficient and have replaced hubs in many networks.

questions.question: Why is a switch generally better than a hub?
options: It sends data to the correct device instead of broadcasting to all devices
It is only used in satellite networks
questions.answer: It sends data to the correct device instead of broadcasting to all devices
questions.correctAnswer: It sends data to the correct device instead of broadcasting to all devices
questions.explanation:
A switch forwards data more intelligently to the intended device.
This improves performance and reduces unnecessary traffic.

questions.question: Which device interconnects two similar networks and decides whether to forward or discard signals?
questions.explanation:
A bridge connects similar networks and inspects incoming frames/signals to decide forwarding.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which device determines the best path for data transmission using IP address?
questions.explanation:
A router joins multiple networks and uses IP addressing to choose paths for data transmission.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A repeater is mainly used to:
questions.explanation:
A repeater extends transmission distance by regenerating or amplifying weak signals.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: MODEM stands for:
questions.explanation:
A modem converts digital signals to analog and analog signals to digital.
Its full form is Modulator-Demodulator.

questions.question: Which device converts digital signal into analog and analog signal back into digital?
questions.explanation:
A modem performs modulation and demodulation.
It helps devices communicate over certain communication lines.

questions.question: Which device is most suitable for connecting a LAN to the Internet?
questions.explanation:
A router connects different networks and commonly connects a LAN to Internet/WAN.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which device is simplest and low-cost but inefficient because it broadcasts?
questions.explanation:
A hub is simple and cheaper but sends data to all connected devices, increasing traffic.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which device uses multiple ports and joins computers in a star topology more efficiently than a hub?
questions.explanation:
A switch connects multiple devices in a LAN, often forming a star topology around it.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A company has two LAN segments using similar protocols and wants to interconnect them. Which device fits best?
questions.explanation:
A bridge is designed to connect similar network segments and filter/forward traffic.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Router - chooses best path using IP
Hub - sends data only to one selected port always
questions.answer: Router - chooses best path using IP
questions.correctAnswer: Router - chooses best path using IP
questions.explanation:
Routers use IP addresses and route data through appropriate paths between networks.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: What is a key performance benefit of using fiber with media converters?
questions.explanation:
Fiber provides higher speed and less interference.
Converters help copper networks connect to fiber links.

questions.question: A device receives a weak signal and sends it again stronger. Which device is described?
questions.explanation:
Repeaters regenerate or amplify signals to extend communication range.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which device is most intelligent among hub, switch, and router in choosing paths between networks?
questions.explanation:
Routers work across networks using IP addresses.
They can determine suitable routes for packets.

questions.question: Network topology means:
options: The speed of mobile Internet only
Physical or logical arrangement of devices and links in a network
questions.answer: Physical or logical arrangement of devices and links in a network
questions.correctAnswer: Physical or logical arrangement of devices and links in a network
questions.explanation:
Network topology describes how nodes, cables, and links are arranged.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which list contains topology types from the notes?
questions.explanation:
The notes include bus, star, ring, and hybrid topology.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: In bus topology, all nodes are connected to:
questions.explanation:
Bus topology uses one main cable/backbone to which all nodes connect.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which component is necessary at both ends of a bus topology cable?
questions.explanation:
Terminators are needed at both ends of the bus cable to prevent signal reflection.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is a major disadvantage of bus topology?
options: A single backbone cable failure can stop the whole network
questions.answer: A single backbone cable failure can stop the whole network
questions.correctAnswer: A single backbone cable failure can stop the whole network
questions.explanation:
In bus topology, the main cable is a critical point.
If it fails, the entire network may stop.

questions.question: Why does bus topology become slower as more devices are added?
options: More devices increase traffic on the shared main cable
questions.answer: More devices increase traffic on the shared main cable
questions.correctAnswer: More devices increase traffic on the shared main cable
questions.explanation:
All devices share the same backbone.
More devices create more traffic and reduce performance.

questions.question: Star topology connects all nodes to:
questions.explanation:
In star topology, each node connects separately to a central hub or switch.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is the most serious weakness of star topology?
options: Failure of central hub/switch can stop the whole network
One computer failure always stops all others
questions.answer: Failure of central hub/switch can stop the whole network
questions.correctAnswer: Failure of central hub/switch can stop the whole network
questions.explanation:
The central device is the main dependency.
If it fails, the star network may stop working.

questions.question: Which advantage belongs to star topology?
options: Easy troubleshooting and one node failure does not affect others
Main cable failure is always hidden
questions.answer: Easy troubleshooting and one node failure does not affect others
questions.correctAnswer: Easy troubleshooting and one node failure does not affect others
questions.explanation:
Star topology is easy to set up and troubleshoot.
Failure of one computer does not normally affect the rest.

questions.question: Ring topology connects devices:
options: In a circular loop where each device connects to two other devices
To a single bus cable with terminators
questions.answer: In a circular loop where each device connects to two other devices
questions.correctAnswer: In a circular loop where each device connects to two other devices
questions.explanation:
Ring topology forms a closed loop.
Each node links with two neighboring nodes.

questions.question: In ring topology, data generally travels:
options: From one node to another in sequence
questions.answer: From one node to another in sequence
questions.correctAnswer: From one node to another in sequence
questions.explanation:
Data passes from one node to the next in order around the loop.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is a feature of ring topology from the notes?
options: Each node can act as a repeater to forward data
It uses one central hub only
questions.answer: Each node can act as a repeater to forward data
questions.correctAnswer: Each node can act as a repeater to forward data
questions.explanation:
Each node in a ring can forward data to the next node, acting like a repeater.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is a disadvantage of ring topology?
options: Adding/removing a device can disturb the network
It is always faster than all topologies
questions.answer: Adding/removing a device can disturb the network
questions.correctAnswer: Adding/removing a device can disturb the network
questions.explanation:
Changing a ring can disturb the loop.
A failure may affect the whole network.

questions.question: Hybrid topology is:
options: Combination of two or more different topologies
questions.answer: Combination of two or more different topologies
questions.correctAnswer: Combination of two or more different topologies
questions.explanation:
Hybrid topology combines topologies such as star, bus, and ring into one network.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which organization is most likely to use hybrid topology?
options: Large institution/company with different network sections
questions.answer: Large institution/company with different network sections
questions.correctAnswer: Large institution/company with different network sections
questions.explanation:
Hybrid topology is useful for large organizations because different sections may require different designs.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is an advantage of hybrid topology?
options: It can be customized and expanded according to organization needs
questions.answer: It can be customized and expanded according to organization needs
questions.correctAnswer: It can be customized and expanded according to organization needs
questions.explanation:
Hybrid topology is flexible and scalable.
It can combine best features of different designs.

questions.question: Which is a disadvantage of hybrid topology?
questions.explanation:
Hybrid networks need more planning, devices, cables, and skilled maintenance.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A network is cheap and easy for a small setup but difficult to troubleshoot and dependent on one backbone. Which topology is it?
questions.explanation:
Bus topology is cheap and simple but has backbone dependency and fault detection problems.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A network has a switch at the center and each computer has a separate cable. Which topology?
questions.explanation:
Star topology uses a central device with separate links to each node.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which topology has the best description: 'ring section plus star section connected together'?
questions.explanation:
Combining ring and star sections creates a hybrid topology.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A computer network is:
options: A group of connected computers/devices that exchange data and share resources
questions.answer: A group of connected computers/devices that exchange data and share resources
questions.correctAnswer: A group of connected computers/devices that exchange data and share resources
questions.explanation:
A computer network connects two or more devices through wired or wireless media for data sharing and resource sharing.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which resource can be shared in a computer network?
options: Files, Internet, storage, hardware and software
questions.answer: Files, Internet, storage, hardware and software
questions.correctAnswer: Files, Internet, storage, hardware and software
questions.explanation:
Networks allow sharing of data and resources such as files, printers, Internet, storage, and software.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: PAN usually covers:
options: Very small range around a person
questions.answer: Very small range around a person
questions.correctAnswer: Very small range around a person
questions.explanation:
Personal Area Network connects personal devices within a very small range, often around 10 meters.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is the best example of PAN?
questions.explanation:
PAN connects nearby personal devices such as phones, smartwatches, laptops, keyboards, and earbuds.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: LAN is best described as a network covering:
options: A room, building, school, or office
questions.answer: A room, building, school, or office
questions.correctAnswer: A room, building, school, or office
questions.explanation:
Local Area Network connects devices in a small geographical area such as a school or office.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which feature best belongs to LAN?
options: High-speed data transfer in a small area
Lowest speed due to global distance
questions.answer: High-speed data transfer in a small area
questions.correctAnswer: High-speed data transfer in a small area
questions.explanation:
LANs usually provide high speed over small areas and are easy to install/maintain.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: MAN covers an area such as:
options: A city, valley, or metropolitan area
questions.answer: A city, valley, or metropolitan area
questions.correctAnswer: A city, valley, or metropolitan area
questions.explanation:
Metropolitan Area Network covers a larger area than LAN but smaller than WAN.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which statement about MAN is most accurate?
options: It connects multiple LANs and can cover a city
It never needs wire or wireless media
It cannot be owned by organizations
questions.answer: It connects multiple LANs and can cover a city
questions.correctAnswer: It connects multiple LANs and can cover a city
questions.explanation:
MAN connects multiple LANs across a city or campus-like area.
It may be owned by one or more organizations.

questions.question: WAN is mainly used to connect:
options: Large geographical areas such as countries or continents
questions.answer: Large geographical areas such as countries or continents
questions.correctAnswer: Large geographical areas such as countries or continents
questions.explanation:
Wide Area Network covers very large geographical areas and can connect LANs and MANs.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is the best example of WAN from the notes?
questions.explanation:
The Internet is the best-known WAN because it connects networks across the world.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which network type generally has the largest coverage?
questions.explanation:
WAN has the widest geographical coverage among PAN, LAN, MAN, and WAN.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which order is correct from smallest to largest coverage?
questions.explanation:
PAN is personal range, LAN is local, MAN is city/metropolitan, and WAN is country/worldwide.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Why is WAN more complex to manage and secure than LAN?
options: It covers large areas and may use many service providers and public networks
It always uses a single cable in one room
questions.answer: It covers large areas and may use many service providers and public networks
questions.correctAnswer: It covers large areas and may use many service providers and public networks
questions.explanation:
WAN connects distant networks and often uses public communication systems, making management and security harder.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A school computer lab with computers connected through a switch is most likely a:
questions.explanation:
A school lab network is within a small local area, so it is a LAN.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: A smartwatch, mobile phone, and Bluetooth earbuds connected around one person form a:
questions.explanation:
These devices are personal and close range, so they form a PAN.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Network architecture refers to:
options: Design and structure defining how network devices communicate and interact
Only the color of network cables
questions.answer: Design and structure defining how network devices communicate and interact
questions.correctAnswer: Design and structure defining how network devices communicate and interact
questions.explanation:
Network architecture defines the arrangement, roles, and interaction of devices in a network.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Client-server architecture has:
options: Clients requesting services from one or more servers
All computers completely equal with no server
questions.answer: Clients requesting services from one or more servers
questions.correctAnswer: Clients requesting services from one or more servers
questions.explanation:
In client-server architecture, clients request services/resources and servers provide them.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is a feature of client-server architecture?
options: Better centralized security and organized backup
questions.answer: Better centralized security and organized backup
questions.correctAnswer: Better centralized security and organized backup
questions.explanation:
Client-server networks store/control data centrally, supporting better security and backup.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Which is a disadvantage of client-server architecture?
options: If the main server fails, clients may lose access to services
It is always free and maintenance-free
questions.answer: If the main server fails, clients may lose access to services
questions.correctAnswer: If the main server fails, clients may lose access to services
questions.explanation:
Clients depend on the server.
Server failure can stop access to files, login, printing, or applications.

questions.question: Why can client-server architecture be expensive?
options: It may require a powerful server, devices, licensed software, and trained staff
questions.answer: It may require a powerful server, devices, licensed software, and trained staff
questions.correctAnswer: It may require a powerful server, devices, licensed software, and trained staff
questions.explanation:
A server-based network needs more powerful hardware/software and skilled administration.
It matches the key concept asked in this MCQ.

questions.question: Peer-to-peer architecture means:
options: All computers are equal and can act as both client and server
Only one server controls all clients
questions.answer: All computers are equal and can act as both client and server
